title: How many states carry each employment-law overlay, as the compilations read in October 2026 list them
caption: Counts of states carrying a statewide rule in each of the nine overlays of the state records, taken from the dated compilations each overlay rests on: the pay-transparency and salary-history maps [207](#cite:207) [76](#cite:76), the noncompete tracker [209](#cite:209) with Washington's 2026 statute [210](#cite:210), the stay-or-pay map [211](#cite:211), the AI chart [220](#cite:220), the cannabis page [219](#cite:219), the fair-chance guides [216](#cite:216) [217](#cite:217), the credit-check guide [218](#cite:218) and the mini-WARN chart [214](#cite:214) [213](#cite:213). The District of Columbia is counted in the note column where it carries the rule.
how_to_read: Each bar is the number of states whose law the compilation lists as statewide on the date it was read; the note beside each bar in the data file says what is pending and which states joined in 2026. A short bar is not a safe assumption for any one state: the state record is where to look, and almost every row of it rests on a compilation rather than the statute, which the record says in its primary_pending flag.

explain.text: A rule the compilation lists as applying across the state to private employers; local ordinances (New York City, Chicago, Philadelphia, the Ohio cities) are in the localities line of the state records and not counted here [207](#cite:207) [218](#cite:218).

Washington's noncompete ban takes effect on 2027-06-30 [210](#cite:210); New York's stay-or-pay act on 2027-02-13 [211](#cite:211); Colorado, Connecticut and Delaware's AI duties in 2027 [220](#cite:220).

source: Counted by the builder from states.yaml on 2026-10-22, where each state record cites the compilation behind it; the compilations are law-firm, vendor and advocacy pages, and the statutes themselves are a listed todo. No state law was read for this figure except Washington's two session laws and Colorado's fiscal note.
